precepts.text: To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness. So the Lord referred to us as trees of righteousness. In Psalms 1 it referred to us as trees whose leaves not going to wither, meaning those trees is healthy, those trees is nourished.
precepts.point: Planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither. What kind of tree does not bear fruit and its leaves wither? A tree that's unhealthy. A tree that is unhealthy is going to wither and fade away. It's the same analogy for us as human beings that God created from the earth. A tree need water, a tree need sun, a tree need nourishment from the earth. The same way how we take nourishment from the earth.
precepts.why:
Psalms 1 says the blessed man, whose delight is in the law of the Lord, “shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither.” The Bible says we came from the ground, and the scripture says we are going to be like a tree. Everything is symbolic; there's a reason why God referred to us as trees.

Isaiah shows it: “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness.” The Lord refers to us as trees of righteousness.

In Psalms 1 he refers to us as trees whose leaves are not going to wither, meaning those trees are healthy, those trees are nourished. What kind of tree doesn't bear fruit and its leaves wither? A tree that's unhealthy, and an unhealthy tree is going to wither and fade away. It's the same analogy for us as human beings that God created from the earth. A tree needs water, a tree needs sun, a tree needs nourishment from the earth, the same way we take nourishment from the earth.

precepts.point: The tree of life stood in the midst of the garden.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Psalm 1 was read from the top: “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season”.

The man who delights in the law is the tree. He is planted by rivers of water and brings forth fruit. That is what the trees of the garden are: the righteous, the planting of the Lord, bringing forth fruit.

Going back to Genesis 2:9 with that in mind, the trees “pleasant to the sight and good for food” are Adam's sons in the heavens. The rivers of water point to the next verse: “And a river went out of Eden to water the garden”. The trees stand by the river, and that is Adam's governance: the righteous planted by the waters of God's wisdom, in the heavens and on the earth.

precepts.text: Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the ungodly but meditates in the law day and night; he brings forth fruit, meaning action, his spirit does not wither, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.
precepts.point: For then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success: only after the mouth, the meditation, and the doing does prosperity follow. Thus saith God, the second you transgress the commandments of the Lord you cannot prosper, so any pastor teaching prosperity while saying the law is done away with is teaching a lie. Real prosperity never came from sowing a seed into a basket; it comes from obeying the laws of the Most High, and that applies to us as a whole nation of people.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.” The blessed man walks not in the counsel of the ungodly but meditates in the law day and night, the very words the Lord spoke to Joshua.

“And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.” He brings forth fruit, meaning action; his spirit does not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper. That is “then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success”: the true prosperity doctrine.

precepts.text: The ungodly are like the chaff which the wind driveth away, tied to the wind of destruction in Job 27, the nuclear destruction and the winds held back in Revelation.
precepts.point: Wisdom and understanding are hid from all living and given only to the few, the remnant of Israel who have the conscience and the ability to choose whom they will serve, not the other nations; we fear the Lord like King David, the greatest warrior to ever fight on the earth, who still trembled at God's judgments.

note.label: Job 28: Where Shall Wisdom Be Found

precepts.why:
Those without the fear of the Lord have no wisdom: “The ungodly are not so: but are like the chaff which the wind driveth away.”

That wind ties to the wind of destruction in Job 27, the nuclear destruction, and the winds held back in Revelation. The Lord makes the weight for the winds; the ungodly, who do not depart from evil, are the chaff that wind drives away, while wisdom and understanding stay with the few who fear him.

precepts.text: Meditate in the law day and night and observe to do it, and then your way shall be prosperous and you shall have good success, which is the same promise given to the blessed man.
precepts.point: The Most High knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the ungodly shall perish. This is a reminder as we walk through these last days not to roll with ungodly people or anyone who is halfway in and halfway out, because the Most High deals only with those walking righteously. You cannot excuse a work Christmas party as just appeasing people, because the righteous do everything they can to walk in the way of the godly and make no excuses.

note.label: Psalm 1: Blessed Is the Man That Walketh Not in the Counsel of the Ungodly

precepts.why:
“And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.” The same promise was given to Joshua, with the condition spelled out: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.”

Meditate in the law day and night and observe to do it, and then your way shall be prosperous and you shall have good success. That is the blessed man's prosperity: it comes from meditating in the commandments day and night and doing them.

You will be successful and prosper if you actually meditate in the commandments day and night and do them, not merely think about scriptures the way many of us did in Christianity. The ungodly are not so; they will not prosper like the righteous, but are like the chaff which the wind drives away.

precepts.text: The blessed man delights in the law and meditates day and night, and is like a tree planted by the rivers of water whose leaf shall not wither.
precepts.point: We praise the Most High among the nations now by wearing the fringes and beautiful garments, pushing the gospel in the streets to our people, waking up the dead state of our people while Bishop destroys Christianity week after week.
precepts.why:
“My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed: I will sing and give praise.” A fixed heart is the tree planted by the rivers of water that will not be swayed. “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.”

“And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.” Doctrines will not pull that man out; he will not be hasty to credit somebody by their looks or their money, and no one takes his crown. David in the spirit says his heart is fixed even though all these enemies come against him, and he awakes early to praise. We praise the Most High among the nations now by wearing the fringes and the beautiful garments, pushing the gospel in the streets to our people, waking up the dead state of our people while Bishop destroys Christianity week after week.

precepts.text: Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the ungodly but delights in the law; that wisdom and patience do not come overnight.
precepts.point: People will come, even family members, saying no one is coming to save you and you must save yourself with guns. You must stay steadfast and answer the Most High's cry with patience.

note.label: Isaiah 30: Woe to the Rebellious Children Who Trust in Egypt

precepts.why:
“Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.” The one who waits for the Most High does not take the counsel of the ungodly, even when it comes from family members saying no one is coming to save you and you must save yourself with guns; his delight is in the law.

“And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season”. A tree brings forth its fruit in its season, not before: that wisdom and patience do not come overnight. Meditate in his law day and night, hold patience through the trials and tribulations, and “whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.” That is what it is to be blessed waiting for him.

precepts.text: The ungodly are like the chaff which the wind driveth away.
precepts.point: He will gather his wheat into the garner and burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire. There are two baptisms in view, and everyone receives one of them.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
John says of the one coming after him, “he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.” Who is the chaff? “The ungodly are not so: but are like the chaff which the wind driveth away.”

The ungodly are the chaff. There are two baptisms in view, the Holy Ghost and fire, and everyone receives one of them. The wheat is gathered into the garner; the chaff, the ungodly, is driven away and burned up with unquenchable fire.
